column3: “With her heart” is rendered “in her heart.”
“Told her all her words” is rendered “answered all her questions.”
The Hebrew reads “his burnt offerings which he offered”; NASB has “his stairway by which he went up,” as in some ancient versions. “Standing” is rendered “attendance.”
“Truth was the word” is rendered “It was a true report.”
The Hebrew reads “your people” (some ancient versions “your wives”); NASB has “your men.”
“According to the hand of the king” is rendered “according to his royal bounty.”
NASB reverses “merchants” and “traders”; the Hebrew is uncertain.
“Body shields” is rendered “large shields,” and NASB supplies “shekels.”
“Monkeys and apes” is rendered “apes and peacocks”; the meaning of the animal names is uncertain.
“The matter of a year in a year” is rendered “so much year by year.”
NASB supplies “as common as” and “as plentiful as.”
“Export” is rendered “import”; the Hebrew is uncertain. “Que” is spelled “Kue.”
